incident_flags.snippet: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead if circumstances permitted.
When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead if circumstances permitted.

runs.steward_comment: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead if circumstances permitted.  She said in accordance with her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages, however, AWESOME FLUKE took some time to muster speed which resulted in a number of runners crossing her mount in the early stages.  She said when left without cover near the 1400 Metres AWESOME FLUKE then commenced to race keenly and her intention was to endeavour to obtain a position with cover behind DEFINITIVE.  She said when CALIFORNIATOTALITY maintained its position one-off behind DEFINITIVE, this resulted in AWESOME FLUKE being obliged to race wide and without cover.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to go forward from the 1300 Metres having regard to the early stages being run outside of standard time, Apprentice Yuen agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect she had made an error of judgement in not allowing her mount to stride forward, particularly as it was racing keenly.  She added that when positioned to the outside of DEFINITIVE she was mindful not to crowd runners to her inside and for this reason she remained racing three wide and without cover from the 900 Metres and into the Home Straight.  Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were to go forward and agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect Apprentice Yuen should have taken the initiative to go forward and cross DEFINITIVE.  When questioned regarding the tactics adopted on the stablemate CHILL EASY, Mr Yiu advised that he had expected the horse to hold a midfield position and was surprised that AWESOME FLUKE remained three deep during the race, particularly from barrier 6 having regard to the instructions.  He said it was not the intention of the stable for this to occur and in the circumstances it was Apprentice Yuen’s riding which led to CHILL EASY being able to obtain cover behind AWESOME FLUKE. Last Run (25/10/26 ST / Turf / "A" 1600m): Fin 04 (LBW 1-3/4) | RunPos: 5 3 1 4 23/12/2023: Disappointing performance. (Passed: 02/01/2024)

He said after jumping well he was able to ride forward to cross runners to his inside where he was positioned to the outside of LUCKY TWENTY.  He added that when positioned back off LUCKY TWENTY he made a decision to endeavour to find cover behind that runner in order to allow his mount to settle.  He said as he did so M F Poon, rider of LUCKY TWENTY, steadied the pace further and as a consequence DAN ATTACK improved quickly to his outside which resulted in FRIENDS OF SHAJING settling further back.  Trainer W K Mo confirmed the instructions were to go forward with the expected slow early pace.  After considering his explanation and the sectional times of the event which showed the early and middle stages were run outside of standard time, Jockey Chau was advised that he had made an error of judgement in electing to take a position with cover behind LUCKY TWENTY.  He was further advised in similar circumstances he would be expected to show better judgement than what he did on this occasion.

incident_flags.snippet: 2.0 fav, led strong pace, collapsed; substantial blood in trachea; trial + vet required; trainer to add hood. When quest

runs.steward_comment: 2.0 fav, led strong pace, collapsed; substantial blood in trachea; trial + vet required; trainer to add hood. When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead. She said having regard to her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages to ensure JEDI SPURS showed sufficient pace to cross runners to its inside. She said after obtaining a margin in advance of HAPPY PEGASUS in the early stages she then commenced to restrain her mount when she was satisfied that JEDI SPURS would be able to lead as instructed. She said as she commenced to restrain her mount approaching the 1000 Metres JEDI SPURS raced keenly and would not respond to her efforts to set a slower pace. She said making the turn leaving the 900 Metres as she applied more pressure to steady the horse to set a more sustainable pace JEDI SPURS became unbalanced when it got its head up and shifted out and from this point she was unable to control the horse in the lead. She added that soon after entering the Home Straight JEDI SPURS came under pressure before giving ground noticeably over the final 200 Metres. Trainer D A Hayes advised the horse had pleased him leading into the race and was of the opinion JEDI SPURS raced too keenly, particularly when ridden along in the early stages to go forward. He added that he would now place a hood on the horse for its next race start and use the services of a senior rider. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea. The performance of JEDI SPURS was considered disappointing. Before being allowed to race again, JEDI SPURS will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. Sent for sampling post-race.

runs.steward_comment: raced wide without cover; bumped with Flash Current. Near the 400 Metres was bumped by FLASH CURRENT which attempted to shift out. When questioned K Teetan stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable but not to ride it along in the early stages. He said those instructions were issued as MR COOL had not finished its races off last season when ridden in a forward position. He said at its last start win on 4 October 2026 MR COOL was able to obtain a handy position without being ridden along to do so and his intention was to ride the horse in a similar manner today. He said whilst MR COOL jumped well he was of the opinion he would have had to make too much use of the horse in the early stages to cross runners to his inside and for this reason he elected to restrain his mount to attempt to obtain a position with cover behind PRESTIGE COME. He said when GENIUS BABY and GRAND PATCH improved to his inside he was unable to obtain cover and as a result was obliged to race very wide and without cover in the early stages. He said as the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time he then elected to ride MR COOL forward from the 900 Metres to cross GRAND PATCH where he then raced wide and without cover for the remainder of the middle stages. Trainer F C Lor confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with the ride of Jockey Teetan. After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Teetan that he had made an error of judgement in the early stages in not attempting to cross runners to his inside, particularly when MR COOL had jumped well and the early and middle stages of the event were being run outside of standard time.

He added in the Home Straight his mount was disappointing in the manner in which it finished the race off.  Trainer F C Lor confirmed the instructions were to go forward and, in his opinion, SMART GOLF was disadvantaged by settling back in the field.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of SMART GOLF was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, SMART GOLF will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

When questioned regarding his riding on the Home Turn Z Purton stated that after shifting to the outside of CAN’T GO WON

runs.steward_comment: When questioned regarding his riding on the Home Turn Z Purton stated that after shifting to the outside of CAN’T GO WONG near the 500 Metres his intention was to follow GOLDEN FORTUNE, a last start winner, or alternatively follow KINGLY DEMEANOR into the race.  He said for this reason he continued to shift out with a view to obtaining clear running.  He said as he did so CAN’T GO WONG shifted out which presented a run to his inside, however, he was of the opinion his best option was to continue to follow the fancied runners into the race, particularly as the early stages had been run inside of standard time and he was concerned the leaders would commence to give ground.  He said after following GOLDEN FORTUNE from the 500 Metres that runner did not improve as he had anticipated and for this reason he shifted to its inside to follow KINGLY DEMEANOR.  He said when KINGLY DEMEANOR did not improve sufficiently in the early stages of the Home Straight to provide him with clear running this resulted in STAR BROSE being held up for clear running between the 450 Metres and the 200 Metres where he was able to improve between GOLDEN FORTUNE and KINGLY DEMEANOR.  Sent for sampling post-race.

runs.steward_comment: Jumped awkwardly, resulting in its rider K C Leung becoming unbalanced.  Approaching the 500 Metres was contacted by LO RIDER which shifted out.  Near the 150 Metres K C Leung dropped his whip.  Between the 150 Metres and the 100 Metres raced in restricted room to the inside of SERAPH GABRIEL which shifted in.  When questioned Jockey Leung stated that after settling in a midfield position to the outside of BIG RETURN, when the pace of the event eased near the 1500 Metres his mount became unbalanced when bumped by BIG RETURN which shifted out when being checked.  He said as a result SUPER GOLDENDRAGON then commenced to race keenly and he allowed it to stride forward.  He said as he improved forward the pace of the race increased and when CALL ME MAGNIFIQUE held its position to his inside he was unable to cross that runner approaching the turn near the 900 Metres.  He said as a consequence he elected to remain racing to the outside of CALL ME MAGNIFIQUE before being able to obtain cover near the 700 Metres.  He added that under pressure in the Home Straight his mount finished the race off only fairly which he attributed to the race not being run to suit.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of mucus in the horse’s trachea. runs.steward_comment: severely checked at the post. Near the 700 Metres was steadied when awkwardly positioned to the inside of MIGHTY STEED. The Stewards inquired into the reasons for TOP DRAGON being severely checked between PRAY FOR JUSTICE (K Teetan) and LUCKY SAM GOR (C L Chau) passing the winning post. K Teetan was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that passing the winning post he allowed his mount to shift out, contributing to TOP DRAGON being severely checked between PRAY FOR JUSTICE and LUCKY SAM GOR. In all the circumstances K Teetan was issued with a severe reprimand and advised that in similar circumstances he would be expected to make a greater effort than what he did on this occasion to prevent his mounts from shifting ground. C L Chau was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that passing the winning post he allowed his mount to shift in when insufficiently clear of TOP DRAGON, contributing to TOP DRAGON being severely checked between LUCKY SAM GOR and PRAY FOR JUSTICE. In issuing Jockey Chau with a severe reprimand the Stewards were mindful that LUCKY SAM GOR did shift in quickly which provided Jockey Chau with limited opportunity to straighten his mount. However, the Stewards advised Jockey Chau that he must react with more urgency in similar circumstances to correct his mounts.

C L Chau reported that from the 500 Metres he became concerned there was something amiss with the horse and as a result he elected not to continue to pressure his mount. runs.steward_comment: When questioned regarding his riding in the Home Straight J Orman stated that he followed SPEEDY POWER during the running of the race.  He said after entering the Home Straight when SPEEDY POWER shifted out to improve he made ground to the inside of SPEEDY POWER where he was presented with the option to continue to improve to its inside behind DOUBLE ALPHA.  He said he was reluctant to commit to this position as he was concerned that DOUBLE ALPHA would not take him into the race and therefore he elected to follow SPEEDY POWER.  He said whilst this resulted in YEE CHEONG GLORY having some difficulty obtaining clear running between the 400 Metres and the 300 Metres he felt this was the best option to provide it with clear running.  He added when SPEEDY POWER quickened near the 250 Metres his mount took some time to respond to his riding and after laying in and away from PRIVATE WEALTH when obtaining a narrow run between PRIVATE WEALTH and COPARTNER A I near the 100 Metres he was satisfied with his mount’s finishing effort over the concluding stages.
